page.layout: One printed page (left page, page 2) with running head above and a catchword at the foot. Two headings in italic, centred, each followed by paragraphs. A narrow strip of the facing page is visible at the right edge of the scan; it is the edge of the neighbouring page and is not transcribed. No margin notes on this page.

main_text.p: Quod Hebræi voce Berith, significante pactionem seu fedus, à barath .i. fedus inire, denotant, id Græci διαθηκην .i. dispositio-nem, Latini vero Testamentum appellant. Sed vox Testamenti ambigua est, & hinc non tam vo-luntatem morientis, quam appellant ultimam, quam viventium pacta declarat. Hac signifi-catione dicimus, Testamentum Dei; id est fedus seu pactum, & ordinationem, quam Deus ra-tam haberi voluit: prorsus uti cōditiones & pa-cta percutientium federa, aut quæ morientium extrema voluntate sunt constituta violare ne-phas est.

Cùm autem passim in libris sacris potissi-mum doceatur, quomodo Deus humanum ge-nus promiserit se seruaturum, atque ad id perfi-ciendum missurum etiam semen benedictum, id est proprium & vnigenitum filium IESVM CHRISTVM: rursus vero, quomodo homines qui huius beneficentiæ Dei futuri sunt partici-pes, vicissim obstringantur ad præstandum cer-ta fidei & charitatis officia ad Dei gloriam: ap-positè sanè omnes libri, in quibus his de rebus disseritur, Testamenti appellatione honestan-tur.

EST autem vnicum tantum Dei Testamen-tum, immutabile, æternum, sicut ipse quoque immutabilis atque æternus existit: verùm Testamentum Vetus nominatur pars illa, cui libri accensentur, in quibus modò apertis verbis{a}

page.notes: The reference mark "a" after "verbis" has no matching note on this page. The catchword "modò" is set at the foot, right. The right edge of the scan shows part of the facing page, which is cropped and not transcribed. The drop capitals "Q" and "E" are joined to their words. "Quod" is printed "QVod" and is read as Quod. The word after "ap-" is printed "apositè" with a hyphen at the line end; it is read as ap-positè and is uncertain, so it may be [?]. Otherwise no doubtful readings.
